selected-fill.roleHint: Selected row on the page; a tonal step, no shadow. Light: sand. In the sand drafts column the selected row uses the segment colour instead.

fill-on-surface.roleHint: A shaded box inside a panel (the quiet pill, the chosen place, the layout picker's choices, the icon picker's cells). Light: sand; dark: strong sand. Fields and quiet buttons use Field.

night-selected-fill.roleHint: Selected row in the dark scheme (the selected-segment step).

night-fill-on-surface.roleHint: Fill on Surface in the dark scheme (strong surface).

year-night-selected-fill.roleHint: Selected row in the yearly palette, dark scheme.

device-bezel.roleHint: Phone frame bezel ring and cutout only; device hardware, never a UI colour.

on-masthead-2.roleHint: Resting links in the admin sidebar, on navy.

masthead-chip.roleHint: Ghost-on-masthead fills, the admin sidebar Jump to field, current link and hover (at 60%), the rule above the sidebar foot group, the failed-pins line and the narrow window Menu button. 10% in dark.

live.roleHint: The live fill in light (Watch while streaming, switch on); white on it holds 4.8:1.

field.roleHint: Fields (with Field Edge), quiet buttons, filter chips, the segmented track, steppers and the switch's off track. Light: sand.

field-edge.roleHint: The 1px inset edge of a field: ink-3 at 70%. Focus replaces it with the 2px deep-aqua ring.

night-field.roleHint: Field in dark: the panel lifted 7% towards white, worked out the same in every theme.

night-field-edge.roleHint: Field Edge in dark: night-ink-3 at 70%.

display.purpose: Masthead title on every tab root.

display-year.purpose: Masthead title under the 2026 yearly palette only.

prose.purpose: Welcome letter and descriptions, max 65ch, ink-2.

micro.purpose: Tab-bar labels, unread badge, day-rail weekdays; uppercase admin sidebar Pinned and Everything labels, the Jump to key hint (not uppercase) and office-week weekdays.

pill.purpose: Pills, admin sidebar count capsules and area page counts, office-week capsule dates. The label line over a special in the agenda and on an event head.

code.purpose: Permission nodes and patterns in the admin developer roles tool only.

date-numeral.purpose: The day of the month in an event's date block (2rem, 700, tabular); headline size in the compact block.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Boxed lists and the event feature card only (light scheme).

shadows.name: lift-dark
shadows.purpose: The same lift in the dark scheme.

shadows.name: segment
shadows.purpose: Selected segment of the segmented control.

shadows.name: play-overlay
shadows.purpose: Round play button over a video hero.

shadows.name: badge-ring
shadows.purpose: Separates the unread badge from the bell.

shadows.name: frosted-bar
shadows.value: backdrop-filter: saturate(1.6) blur(18px); background: 90% page colour; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 var(--line)
shadows.purpose: Section tabs (tab bar uses saturate(1.8) blur(20px) and a top hairline).

shadows.name: device-frame
shadows.purpose: The phone frame: a 9px bezel ring drawn as a spread, then the lift.

shadows.name: drag-lift
shadows.value: filter: drop-shadow(0 18px 26px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 30%, transparent)); scale: 1.04 while moving
shadows.purpose: A Home tile while it is moved or resized on the admin Hub canvas, nowhere else.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Menus, popovers and the chip picker's matches: anything that opens over the page from a button.

shadows.name: pop-wide
shadows.purpose: The Account menu and the date and time popovers.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single curve for presses, sheets, the section-tab underline and page entry.

motion.name: paged-turn
motion.purpose: A paged sheet's cover and body on a page change only; never on first open.

motion.name: page-dot
motion.value: 240ms ease-out, width 8px to 20px and line to orange
motion.purpose: The current page dot widening to a capsule.

motion.name: reduced-motion

motion.name: sidebar-area-fold
motion.value: 200ms ease-out: the chevron rotates 0 to 90deg; the area's pages fade in from opacity 0 and translateY(-4px)

motion.name: admin-hover
motion.value: 160ms background-color and color, ease-out (120ms for table rows)
motion.purpose: Admin sidebar links, area heads, pin buttons and the Jump to field, filter chips, area rows, table rows.

motion.name: sort-arrow
motion.purpose: Data-table sort arrow appearing on hover.

motion.name: calendar-fills
motion.value: 160ms ease-out (week rail), 140ms ease-out curve (month grid, rich text toolbar)

breakpoints.name: admin-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Admin sidebar becomes a sticky strip with the mark, the name and a Menu button; the menu opens the same sidebar as a navy panel up to 320px wide under the strip, over the scrim.

breakpoints.name: admin-office-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Office week columns stack; the seven-day rail scrolls sideways (days at least 84px); the announcements desk drops its proof under the writing column; the Feedback board's docked ticket leaves the grid and floats over the board at the right edge (980px work area + 248px sidebar).

breakpoints.name: admin-access-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Access page stacks its role column above the place.

breakpoints.name: table-optional-columns
breakpoints.purpose: Optional table columns hide when the split-view list is narrower.

breakpoints.name: sheet-centred
breakpoints.purpose: Sheets centre on the screen; a sheet without a cover hides its grabber.

breakpoints.name: feedback-ticket-page-stack
breakpoints.purpose: A Feedback ticket opened as a page drops its side under its main column.

breakpoints.name: workbench-record-narrows
breakpoints.purpose: The record pane narrows to 320 to 380px and the rail moves above the list, or folds away with FoldAside while a record is open.

breakpoints.name: workbench-one-pane
breakpoints.purpose: The workbench shows one pane at a time; the split view's form stacks the record under the list.

breakpoints.name: save-bar-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: A save bar's other actions move to their own line above Cancel and Save.

themes.default: light scheme, brand palette; Appearance setting defaults to Automatic (follows the system)
themes.year: 2026 yearly palette, under comparison with the brand palette; swaps greens and a DM Serif Text masthead title

extensions.rootType: html font: -apple-system-body when supported, else 17px; all sizes in rem

deviceGeometry.purpose: Phone frame hardware shapes; not part of the radius scale and never used on UI boxes.

dayRail.purpose: The shared office-week rail (DayRail): a week on the admin home page, a fortnight on Announcements.
dayRail.week: 7 days from today; columns minmax(0,1fr), at least 84px and scrolling sideways at 1228px and under.
dayRail.fortnight: 14 days from this week's Monday; columns at least 56px, 6px gap, 8px 8px 10px day padding, capsules 5px 7px in pill type; scrolls sideways when the days don't fit.
dayRail.packing: each capsule takes the highest band where it doesn't touch another
dayRail.moment: a span whose end equals its start reserves its day and the next two (clipped at the rail's end), shows a two-line title and the time alone

hubGrid.narrowTile: at 112px or less: no lines, title at label size, 12px padding
hubGrid.smallTile: at 200px or less: play disc 40px in the top corner, trailing icon hidden on picture and beside, agenda time stacked above the event, unread-dot titles up to 2 lines
hubGrid.posterIcon: 52px when the poster is 240px wide or more
hubGrid.canvasGlide: 200ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) after a 110ms dwell; landing slot outline 2px dashed var(--marker) on marker at 12%; column guides ink at 18% only while dragging

calendar.purpose: The church calendar (Events): one running diary from today; the ordinary stays quiet and only what is different speaks.
calendar.weekBand: Sticky at var(--top-h) + var(--sat), z-index 19, masthead ground, padding 0 var(--gutter) 14px; the masthead above it ends with 14px padding; the top bar turns solid after 90px.
calendar.agendaTimeColumn: 4.75rem, label size, 600, tabular, primary; quiet and not-on rows at 400 in ink-3.

monthMarks.onToday: regular on-primary 50%, special on-primary, ring on-primary

dateBlock.light: surface tile (white) with primary numerals, weekday ink-3
dateBlock.dark: surface tile (night-surface) with primary numerals (bright aqua): a dark tile with aqua numerals

calendar.changeNote: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--marker) 22%, transparent); 12px radius; 11px 14px; caption in ink; lead in marker-ink 700
calendar.wideningAsk: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--marker) 18%, transparent); 12px radius; 11px 14px
calendar.editorFoot: position: sticky; bottom: -32px (docked on the tab bar); var(--bar) with backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.4); hairline top; in the admin panel sticky bottom 0 on var(--surface), 14px 16px 16px, no blur. Save (primary, block) beside Not on this date (quiet); never a This date only | Every … choice (owner, 2026-11-08).

dateStrip.tile: 56px wide, 8px gap, var(--radius-field), surface with primary tabular numerals; weekday micro 700 +0.06em ink-3; day title size 700; month micro 700
dateStrip.changed: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--marker) 30%, var(--surface)); 7px marker-ink dot top 6px right 6px
dateStrip.notOn: background: none; color: var(--on-masthead); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--on-masthead) 45%, transparent)
dateStrip.more: after 13 dates, a More dates tile on var(--masthead-chip)
dateStrip.key: caption in var(--masthead-note); 9px swatches: marker dot for changed, inset 1.5px masthead-note ring for not on

calendar.dateOf: The band under a date's head: var(--sand), 12px var(--gutter), caption in ink, repeat icon ink-2, link in accent 700. Under a field that differs: caption ink-2 'Usually …' with 'Put it back' in accent 600.
calendar.regularBody: Every date beside How it runs: grid gap 8px 40px, two equal columns from a 760px container; column heads title size 700 -0.015em over an ink-2 caption lead.

tabsCanvas.columns: rail minmax(180px, 200px), 20px gap, then the phone; the workbench's settings column minmax(320px, 400px)
tabsCanvas.phoneTab: each tab a button at the field radius; hover inset 2px marker ring at 60%, chosen the full inset 2px marker ring over 160ms; More at 60% opacity, not choosable
tabsCanvas.row: 44px sand at the field radius, numbered in tabular ink-3; chosen turns surface with the inset 2px marker ring; More last as a 1px line outline with a lock

components.css: .ds-section-tabs { display: flex; gap: 18px; padding: 0 20px; overflow-x: auto; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.9); backdrop-filter: saturate(1.6) blur(18px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 var(--line, rgb(42 61 94 / 0.12)); font-family: "Montserrat", -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-section-tabs button { position: relative; flex: none; padding: 14px 0 12px; border: 0; background: none; font: inherit; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-3, #626a79); cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms; } .ds-section-tabs button:hover, .ds-section-tabs button.on { color: var(--ink, #18233a); } .ds-section-tabs button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #00776d); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-section-tabs i { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--marker, #e7ae74); transition: transform 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); }

components.name: List rows
components.description: Hairline-divided rows: leading tile, title and caption, trailing chevron; an unread row has a 9px marker dot in a 17px gutter and a 700 title, a read row a 500 title.

components.css: .ds-list { border-top: 1px solid var(--line, rgb(42 61 94 / 0.12)); font-family: "Montserrat", -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; min-height: 56px; padding: 12px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, rgb(42 61 94 / 0.12)); color: var(--ink-3, #626a79); text-decoration: none; transition: background 120ms; } .ds-row:hover, .ds-row:active { background: var(--line, rgb(42 61 94 / 0.12)); } .ds-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #00776d); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-row-icon { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 34px; height: 34px; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--sand, #f4efe7); color: var(--primary, #2a3d5e); flex: none; } .ds-row-body { flex: 1; min-width: 0; } .ds-row-title { display: block; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15.5px; line-height: 1.3; color: var(--ink, #18233a); } .ds-row-title.ds-unread { font-weight: 700; } .ds-row-sub { display: block; margin-top: 2px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--ink-2, #545e70); } .ds-row-icon--warm { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--marker, #e7ae74) 30%, transparent); color: var(--marker-ink, #8a5422); } .ds-row-title.ds-unread { position: relative; padding-left: 17px; } .ds-dot { position: absolute; top: 0.42em; left: 0; width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--marker, #e7ae74); } .ds-action { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; margin-top: 6px; color: var(--accent, #00776d); font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Passage chips and pill
components.description: Bible passage capsules under sermon outline points, and the pill in its Marker, Accent and Quiet tones.

components.name: Filter chips
components.description: Sand capsules; the selected one turns navy.

components.name: Field
components.description: Field fill with a fine field edge, a caption label, an ink-2 placeholder and the inset deep-aqua focus ring in place of the edge.

components.name: Segmented control

components.name: Tab strip with counts

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Sunday Bulletin"**

The app reads like the church's own printed bulletin brought onto a phone. Every top-level tab opens on a navy masthead carrying a large title, a short line of context in beige, and the faint ring of the church's mark bleeding off the right edge; below it the page turns white and continues as a single readable column, with sand-coloured callouts where the bulletin would use a shaded box. On the long, sectioned pages (Sunday and Listen) a sticky row of section tabs sits under the masthead with an orange underline that slides to the section in view, so the page navigates like a folded bulletin rather than a dashboard.

Density is calm and generous: one column, a 20px gutter, list rows with hairline dividers instead of card stacks, and type sized off the iOS body text setting so the congregation's own Dynamic Type choice carries through. The system rejects the generic church-app template, a uniform grid of identical icon squares, and the feed of identical cards; content sits on the page, and cards appear only where a picture leads (an event, a sermon series). Home is the one tab root laid out as tiles (the Hub, chosen 2026-10-27): a grid the church arranges, where tiles differ in size, tone and content shape, so it reads as the bulletin's front page rather than an app launcher.

Light is the default scheme. An app-wide dark scheme (night navy ground, raised navy surfaces, bright aqua, orange progress) is chosen in Appearance or follows the system. A second palette, the 2026 yearly theme (the website's greens and a serif masthead), is a full alternate. Which one everyone sees is data, not a release: staff choose the year's theme under *The app's colours* on App styling (optionally for a run of dates), an event's colours go in a draft turned on between dates, and anyone who may make that choice can preview the other palette on their own phone first.

The admin panel is the same bulletin carried to the church office's desk. A persistent navy sidebar takes the masthead's place, the work area stays white, and a compact title band replaces the phone masthead. It opens on the office week: the next seven days as a sand rail of white day columns carrying what is dated, then what needs you and the areas you look after. Areas are worked in one workbench: filters in a sand rail where a page has them, the list, and the chosen record ruled off beside it with Cancel and Save at its foot. Each job is done one way, by one shared component, on the phone and on the desk alike. The panel follows the computer's light or dark setting until someone picks Light or Dark in the Account menu.
keyCharacteristics: Navy masthead on every tab root, with the mark's ring echo at 7% opacity.
Sticky section tabs with a sliding orange underline on sectioned pages.
A navy top bar that is transparent over the masthead and turns solid once scrolled past it.
White page, sand callouts, hairline-divided rows; shadows only on the few boxed lists and picture cards.
Montserrat throughout at 400, 600 and 700; DM Serif Text only for yearly-theme mastheads.
rem type tied to the iOS body text size, so Dynamic Type scales the whole app.

In the admin panel, a 248px navy sidebar of Jump to, pinned pages and areas that fold, an orange marker bar on the current page and orange count capsules, over a white work area that opens with a title band.

One way per job (the pattern map): the workbench for a list and its record, Cancel bottom left and Save bottom right, Delete in the item's ⋯ menu, settings in grouped sections, underline tabs for switching views.
Home as the Hub: a 2 to 4 column grid of 14px-radius tiles in theme tones, each tile one of six shapes, sized by the church in columns and rows, under a compact masthead.

The calendar as one running diary: a sticky navy week band with the seven-day rail over day sections of hairline agenda rows, where regular events stay quiet and only what's different (a special, a change, a date that isn't on) speaks; an event opens on a navy head with a white date block, and is edited where it is read; a regular event has a page of its own that opens on its run of dates, and a date of it is changed on its own.

A tab bar built from what features register, ending in More; with the Hub home (favoured 2026-10-27) it grows to Home, Listen, Prayer, More. A notifications bell with an orange unread badge joins every tab root with the inbox.

rules.name: The Roles Not Hexes Rule
rules.body: Components use the semantic roles (masthead, primary, accent, live, marker, sand, ink, line) and never a palette hex, because every role is redefined by the scheme and the yearly theme. The only literal colours in components are the palette-picker swatches, the black video hero, and white on the play overlay.

rules.name: The Marker Rule
rules.body: Orange means "here" or "new": the active section, the unread item, how far you've listened, today on the week rail, an event changed since members last opened it, the tile chosen on the Hub canvas, the next set of Life Groups to fill. It is never a button fill and never decoration. The one ground it may fill is a Home tile in the Highlight or Pale highlight tone (`marker`, `marker-soft`), which staff choose for a tile they want to stand out; no tile ships in solid Highlight by default. The other is a calendar row that stands out (a one-off or a changed date), tinted marker at 14% in the app's week and month lists (owner, 2026-11-09), so it follows the theme as the marker does. On the canvas it also marks the chosen picture in the media chooser.

rules.name: The Aqua Acts Rule
rules.body: Aqua is for live state, for things you can act on (links, passages, the active tab), and for one short line of metadata at most (a series or recurrence line, a "Streamed on YouTube" tag). Navy is for the primary action itself. Don't use aqua for headings or running text.

rules.name: The Contrast Rule
rules.body: Text and placeholders hold 4.5:1 against what they sit on; icons and the edges of controls hold 3:1. The quiet inks (ink-2, ink-3) are worked out to read on the page, on shaded boxes and on fields, in every theme and both schemes. Nothing is faded with opacity to look quiet, past or disabled: it changes colour instead (Buttons, *Disabled*). Opacity is for images and covers, drag ghosts, the mark at 7%, and brief press and busy feedback, and never takes text below these numbers. App styling refuses a theme that breaks it: the theme check measures each text colour against what it sits on, in light and in dark, quiet and secondary text in shaded boxes and in fields, danger text in shaded boxes, the masthead's quieter text and the text on its buttons included.

rules.name: The Dynamic Type Rule
rules.body: Every font size is in rem off the iOS body root. Never set a font size in px; the only px type is the 17px root fallback for platforms without `-apple-system-body`.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Montserrat is the only face on the page. The serif belongs to the yearly palette's masthead title and nowhere else; the monospace belongs to raw permission nodes in the developer roles tool and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Numbers Line Up Rule
rules.body: Times, durations, dates in the day rail and positions use tabular figures; so do the agenda's time column, the week rail, the month grid, the week band's range and an event's when line and date block.

rules.name: The Sidebar Offset Rule
rules.body: Admin breakpoints are window media queries offset by the sidebar's 248px; the workbench's own steps are 1360px and 760px of window. Never make the work area a size container: it becomes the containing block for fixed elements and traps sheets and overlays inside it. A component may still use a container on its own inner list (as the workbench's list pane and the save bar do).

rules.name: The Masthead First Rule
rules.body: Every tab root and every settings page opens on a masthead with a title; long, sectioned pages add sticky section tabs under it. Detail pages with a picture lead with the picture instead (a 16:9 hero under a solid navy top bar). The admin panel has no masthead: its navy is the sidebar, and every page opens on a title band.

rules.name: The Still Frame Rule
rules.body: A page that shows one thing at a time keeps its frame while what it shows changes. App styling's title band keeps its 72px whether it carries the sentence or a draft's save line, its buttons hold their places with the Drafts menu always last at the far right, and the phone and the 400px panel keep their widths whether you look at what everyone sees, the colours, Home or the tab bar; choosing a part changes only what is in the panel. The media library keeps its bars above the split view for the same reason.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: No grids of tiles on a tab root other than Home's Hub, and no uniform icon grid anywhere: the Hub's tiles differ in size, tone and shape. Beyond the Hub, the only multi-column layouts are the two-up series grid on Listen and the day rail. On the desk the admin panel adds its shell, the day rail (a week or a fortnight) and the office week's two columns, the workbench (the split view included), the announcements desk's writing and proof columns, the Places explorer's directory and phone, App styling's phone and panel, a board's columns and its docked ticket (and a ticket page's main column and side), and the media library's folder tiles and picture grid (the folders and files themselves, not tools), and still no grid of tool tiles.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Rows, callouts, the sermon head and the player sit flat on the page; only a boxed list, a picture card, a Home tile in the Card tone (`raised`) or the age question on Account (a white card asked once, above Your family, until it is answered) may lift. If something needs separating, give it sand, not a shadow. In the admin panel the only lifted things are the sign-in card, account panels, settings groups (a hairline ring and the lift), the selection tray (docked over a list that scrolls beneath it), menus and popovers (the Pop shadow) and the Feedback board's ticket while it floats over the board under 1228px; tables, the office week, board columns and the workbench's record pane are flat, separated by hairlines and sand, and today on the rail is an inset 2px primary ring, not a shadow. The chosen capsule on the rail, or the current "Not sent yet" chip, is a 2px marker outline at a 2px offset.

rules.name: The Tonal Selection Rule
rules.body: A selected row is marked by a fill one tonal step off its ground (Selected Fill, rounded to the field radius and widened 12px into the gutter on each side, its hairline hidden), never by a shadow or a border. A sand leading tile on a selected row takes the page colour (white in light, night in dark) so it still reads as a tile; an accent tile keeps its tint.

rules.name: The Quiet Regular Rule
rules.body: In the calendar the ordinary stays quiet and only what's different speaks: a regular event is ink-2 at 400 with its time in ink-3 and no label; a special or one-off carries its label in accent and its time in primary; a change is marked in orange until it has been opened; a date that isn't on keeps its place in ink-3 with the circle-off line under its title, never a suffix and never dropped from the list.

rules.name: The One Date Rule
rules.body: A date of a regular event is only that date, and the regular event is changed only on its own page. Never put a switch between "this date" and "every date" in an editor; link the two with words ("One of the Morning service, every Sunday. Edit the regular event ›") and let a date say how it differs from the usual, with Put it back.

rules.name: The App's Own Rule
rules.body: Wherever the app owns something rather than staff (the Made by the app shelf, its folders and crumbs, a file's folder, the shelf's empty state), it carries the lock glyph and one plain caption saying what it is and what staff can't do to it. The lock is ink-2 or the surrounding text colour; ownership takes no colour or badge of its own.

dos: **Do** open every tab root on a masthead with the title in display type, a beige note line and the mark at 7% opacity bleeding off the right edge.
**Do** add sticky section tabs with the sliding orange underline to any long page divided into named sections, and keep every tab label visible at 390pt width.
**Do** put the notifications bell in the top bar of every tab root.
**Do** build content as hairline-divided rows on the white page, and use sand (callouts, sermon head, player, fields) for anything the bulletin would shade.
**Do** size type in rem off the iOS body root and keep Montserrat at 400, 600 and 700.
**Do** read colours through the semantic roles so light, dark and the yearly palette all work without component overrides.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or more and give presses a scale and a haptic.
**Do** mark a selected row with Selected Fill, a tonal step, and nothing else.
**Do** open every admin page on a title band, and work an area in the workbench: filters in the sand rail, the list, the record ruled off beside it.
**Do** put Cancel bottom left and Save bottom right of anything that saves, with its status on its own line above.
**Do** put Delete and every other action on an item in its ⋯ menu, and ask once before deleting, saying what goes with it.
**Do** offset admin breakpoints by the 248px sidebar.
**Do** let staff choose what something opens with the place field and its directory, never by typing an address.
**Do** give a Home tile one of the eight theme tones, and draw it in a layout its kind declares for its size.

**Do** mark the chosen tile on the Hub canvas with the 2px marker ring, its size capsule in words and the corner grip, and warn in plain words only when a tone's text is hard to read in light or dark.
**Do** grey out a layout that doesn't suit a tile and say why, rather than hiding it.
**Do** keep a regular event quiet in the agenda and let only a special, a change or a date that isn't on speak, with a date not on said in a line under its title.
**Do** edit an event where it is read: the same head as a live preview, every change in a field below it, and the save in a foot bar; edit a regular event on its own page, from its run of dates.
**Do** mark whatever the app owns with the lock glyph and one plain caption, and keep a page's bars and path row above its list so choosing an item never moves the list.
**Do** show a safeguarding item that has run out in danger and one due soon in the marker, and never let either block anyone.
**Do** keep a page that shows one thing at a time in one frame (the Still Frame Rule), and put a phone preview's choices under it as one sentence of sand chips that change only the phone.
donts: **Don't** lay a tab root other than Home out as a grid of tiles, and don't let the Hub become a uniform grid of identical icon squares or a feed of identical cards.
**Don't** float buttons over the reading column; actions belong in the top bar, in a section, or in a sheet.
**Don't** use orange as a button fill or decoration; it marks position and newness only.
**Don't** add shadows to rows, callouts or the player; only boxed lists and picture cards lift.
**Don't** use DM Serif Text anywhere but the yearly palette's masthead title.
**Don't** redraw or restyle the church mark beyond recolouring the supplied artwork.
**Don't** put a phone masthead in the admin panel, or open it on a grid of tool tiles.
**Don't** box the workbench's record pane as a card; it is a hairline-ruled column on the page.
**Don't** put a red Delete button in a foot, a save bar or on the page.
**Don't** use the browser's own date or time input in the admin panel, or build a second copy of a pattern the map already has.
**Don't** make the admin work area a size container.
**Don't** mark a date that isn't on with a suffix on its title or by dropping it from the list.
